title: I Challenge a Dev to their OWN Chess Variant (Anarchy Chess)
summary: Tony plays two online games of 'Anarchy Chess' (based on r/AnarchyChess memes) against its developer 'slomg' (~1200 rating), with commentary from both POVs. The 10x10 blue/cream board uses cartoon hand-drawn pieces and many meme rules: underage pawns, knooks from 'nuclear fusion', long passant, bouncing bishops, shared/title rooks, an inverse queen, a checkers piece, and 'bored' pieces that leave the board when you are out of time. Tony wins game 1 (~12:46) and loses game 2 in time-trouble chaos (~21:10).
rules: 10x10 board, meme pieces of r/AnarchyChess (dev slomg plays).
Pawns may move up to three squares (1:06); a pawn can be dragged back onto a piece and launched (1:47, 17:31; not modelled).
Underage pawn: when a move puts it in the line of sight of ANY bishop, own or enemy, that bishop must capture it (0:01, 2:52, 3:38, 4:42).
Nuclear fusion: knight + rook on one square fuse into a Knook (knight + rook up to 2 squares, 7:11); double-click 'super fusion' (20:09, not modelled).
Long passant: en passant captures can be chained (0:01, not modelled).
Bishops bounce off the board edge (5:49, 14:40).
Title (shared) rooks belong to the side with a piece next to them (1:47, 9:44).
Inverse queen moves everywhere a queen does not, i.e. like a knight (6:30).
Checkers piece moves like a checker and can jump over its own pieces (13:56).
No check rule: castling through check is allowed (5:49) and the king can be captured (12:32).
Overtime: when your clock runs out your pieces get bored and leave the board (20:30). Game 2 was 5+0 (12:52).
win_condition: Checkmate/capture the opponent's king (normal chess goal within Anarchy rules).
